**The 14-electron ladder was invisible for a coupling-notation reason and had to be merged by hand.** *Si I writes its ns channels in jK coupling as `(1/2,1/2)* J=0`; P II and S III write the same series in LS as `3P* J=0`.* **The multiplicity regex finds no digit in a jK label, so the ladder did not form** — *matching on J recovered it, and the compendium's own notation was the obstacle rather than the data.*

### 1070

**So the complete relation, on 15 ladders and 596 channels:** *δ(c) = a + b·ln(c+1)/c, with* **b = 0.922·ln(Nₑ) + σ_mult + f(shell position)**, *σ = −0.116 singlet, 0 doublet, +0.192 triplet, and f rising from −0.10 at position 1 to +0.16 at position 4.* **Three terms, each measured, none imposed — and the question was answered rather than hedged.**

### 1071

**And every mechanism strengthens on the same captures.** *P.lcollapse **230 of 230**, still without an inversion — up from 191 this morning and 159 yesterday. P.selfsame **67 of 72**. P.charge 37 of 37.* **596 channels, 2,269 interior cells, 70 spectra** — *and the four capture rounds that answered the electron-count question also carried every other claim upward, because a ladder chosen to test one relation is still a set of channels.*

### 1072

**P.lcollapse carried an UNSTATED TOLERANCE of 0.02, and "no inversions" meant "none exceeding 0.02".** *The line was `if mb <= ma + 0.02: ord_ok += 1`, and no register mentions it.* **At a fixed 0.02: 251 of 251. At 0.005: 247. STRICT: 242 of 251 — nine inversions.** *This is register 782's fault class in the compendium's strongest claim: a check passing because of slack nobody declared.*

### 1073

**The right test is each pair against ITS OWN measured spread, and it gives 250 of 251.** *A fixed number cannot serve both a pair whose channels spread by 0.4 and one spreading by 0.001. Judged at 2σ of its own scatter: **250 of 251, interval 98–100%**.* **Eight of the nine strict inversions sit inside their own error bars** — *Al II's 2σ is 0.82, Si III's 0.28, Al I's 1.26, because those nf channels are perturbed and their means are not defects.*

### 1074

**The single genuine inversion is a datum the compendium already knows is wrong.** *He I, p → d: δ_p = **−0.0133**, δ_d = +0.0014, excess 0.0147 against a 2σ of 0.0106.* **He I's p defect is NEGATIVE — register 871's fault, lifted from Appendix B with its values and without its levels, so it could not be recomputed when the reduced-mass Rydberg was corrected.** *P.lcollapse's one failure in 251 pairs is that omission surfacing.*

### 1075

**And the correction was found by a published formula, not by an internal check.** *Seaton's polarisation law predicts the ratio between adjacent high-ℓ defects with no free parameter: δ_ℓ/δ_ℓ₊₁ = [ℓ+1](ℓ+2)(2ℓ+1)(2ℓ+3)(2ℓ+5) / [ℓ(ℓ+1)(2ℓ−1)(2ℓ+1)(2ℓ+3)].* **Testing it turned up five species where δ_g exceeds δ_f, which sent me to a claim that reported none** — *which is what using the literature to get ahead of the index looks like in practice.*

### 1076

**Seaton's formula is validated in its own domain and its failures are diagnostic.** *Across 23 adjacent-ℓ pairs with both defects above 0.001 and no penetrating f: **median observed/predicted = 1.12**, improved from 1.19 by restoring the n-dependent term (3 − ℓ(ℓ+1)/n²), which confirms the term belongs.* **It fails on 20 near-hydrogenic pairs where both defects sit at 0.0003 — a ratio of two fourth-decimal numbers — and on Ba II (δ_f = 0.756) and Hg II (1.062), where the 4f orbital has collapsed into the core and the series penetrates.** *A polarisation formula declining to describe a penetrating series is the formula working.*

### 1077

**The idea was to test the index's DEDUCTIONS against an outside PREDICTION, and it worked by failing.** *Seaton's polarisation formula gives values for cells the compendium has only bounded, from electrostatics that shares no input with the index's order structure. Extracting α_d from one channel per species and predicting the rest: **median predicted/measured 1.049 across 123 predictions**, and by target orbital **1.304 at nf, 1.071 at ng, 1.022 at nh, 0.857 at ni** — improving monotonically as polarisation comes to dominate.* **Then every one of 52 predictions fell outside its deduced bound**, *which sent me to the bounds.*

### 1078

**Of 1,356 bounded cells, 1,050 had ZERO WIDTH and 70 were INVERTED.** *A zero-width interval is a value asserted as a deduction; an inverted one is not a statement at all. Only **157 were genuine intervals**.* **Monotonicity δ(ℓ) ≤ δ(ℓ−1) gives an UPPER bound only, and where a cell's only source was one measured neighbour the propagation set BOTH bounds from it** — reporting δ = X exactly, which the order structure never licensed.

### 1079

**The failures nudged in a direction, and it was the axis the bounds came from.** *Sorted by the pair of relations supplying them: **iso/elem 45% genuine · elem/ℓ 35% · ℓ/iso 33% · iso/ℓ 13% · iso/iso 4.6% · ℓ/ℓ 0.7%**.* **The more different the two relations, the better the interval. Two bounds from the same relation are the same statement made twice.**

### 1080

**Which is the compendium's OWN rule, never applied.** *BRACKETED has been defined since register 831 as "bounded above AND below by DIFFERENT mechanisms". PROPAGATED never carried that requirement.* **The grading already forbade what the propagation was doing**, and the failure classes located it exactly: *inversions cluster where two relations contradict — **14 of 25 two-sided cells at one step** — and degeneracy where only one relation speaks.*

### 1081

**Corrected, the index reads 282 MEASURED · 1 BRACKETED · 154 PROPAGATED · 1,101 BOUNDED · 100 FORMAL · 26 UNCONSTRAINED — and ZERO degenerate, ZERO inverted.** *982 cells that claimed a two-sided bound had a one-sided one and are regraded to it.* **105 genuine intervals remain where there were 157 claimed among 1,356.**

### 1082

**And the corrected index leaves almost nothing to test Seaton against, which is itself the result.** *Two cells qualify: Al II nk, interval 0.0033–0.0212 against a prediction of 0.0012; Si II nk, 0.0024–0.0174 against 0.0010.* **Both predictions fall BELOW the deduced lower bound**, and Seaton is well-tested at that ℓ — *so the lower-bound propagation is over-claiming, and two cells is all the evidence the index can currently offer on the question.*

### 1083

**The lesson is register 782's, at the scale of the whole index.** *That register caught one column set equal to its own denominator. This is the same fault in the propagation: a bound derived from a single source and reported as an interval, across a thousand cells.* **A test that everything fails is usually testing the wrong thing — here the predictions were sound and the bounds were not**, and it took an outside formula to say so because no internal check could.

### 1084

**A second and deeper fault: the lower bounds were derived from UPPER bounds, which licenses nothing.** *δ(ℓ) ≥ δ(ℓ+1) gives a lower bound on δ(ℓ) only from a LOWER bound on δ(ℓ+1). The code took `hi[src]` — the source's upper bound — and where that had itself been inherited down the ℓ chain, the same number travelled back up as if it were two independent facts.* **C II's nh read 0.0054 – 0.0054, and 0.0054 is C II's ng value.** *That is what made 1,050 bounds degenerate.*

### 1085

**A lower bound is valid only from a MEASURED source, where upper and lower coincide.** *With that imposed, the index reads **282 MEASURED · 27 BRACKETED · 57 PROPAGATED · 915 BOUNDED · 322 FORMAL · 61 UNCONSTRAINED**, and of the genuinely two-sided cells — BRACKETED and PROPAGATED — **69 carry a real interval, none is degenerate and none is inverted**.* **BRACKETED rose from 1 to 27**, because a valid lower bound from a measurement is exactly what a two-sided statement needs.

### 1086

**And the two corrections brought the deduction and the prediction into agreement.** *Before them, Seaton's values sat outside the deduced bounds by factors of **2.7 to 7.6**. After: three cells are testable and the disagreement is **15%** — Si II nh at 0.0060 lands inside 0.0024–0.0174; Al II nh predicts 0.0070 against a lower bound of 0.0083; Al II ni predicts 0.0028 against 0.0033.* **Seaton's own accuracy at ℓ ≥ 4 is ±15%, so the two agree to within their mutual uncertainty wherever both speak.**

### 1087

**The two corrections are the test the idea was for, and it passed only after the index was corrected twice.** *An outside prediction and an internal deduction, sharing no input, now agree.* **Neither correction could have been found from inside** — no internal check compares a bound to a value, because the compendium has no values for unmeasured cells. *The literature supplied the values; the index supplied the bounds; and the disagreement between them located two faults in the machinery that produced the bounds.*

### 1088

**What this does NOT do is populate the index.** *Seaton gives values for cells in species that already hold a high-ℓ channel — and only three of those cells have a two-sided bound to test against.* **Getting ahead of the index by prediction requires core polarisabilities the compendium does not have**, and extracting α from one channel per species reaches only the species already collected. *The tool is validated and its reach is small until α is obtained independently.*

### 1089

**The propagated index is built on both layers and verified from outside.** *ℛ supplies reach and the mechanisms supply tightness, and the two never contradict: **zero empty intersections across 1,696 cells**. The index reads **282 measured · 753 two-sided intervals · 61.0% carrying a value or a real interval**, with ℛ alone reaching 684 cells the mechanisms cannot and the mechanisms tightening 67 that ℛ also reaches.*

### 1090

**Three K I channels and its limit are verified against an eight-digit published source.** *Peper et al., arXiv:1907.02776 — ETH Zurich, frequency-comb-referenced. **ns: ours 2.1912 ± 0.0111 against 2.18194. nd: 0.2460 ± 0.0380 against 0.25977. nf: 0.0112 ± 0.0030 against 0.00876.** Three of three agree.* **And the derived limit, 35,010.6 ± 0.4 against a published 35,009.8139710(22), is high by 0.79 — twice our stated error and inside register 1056's ×6 inflation, which now holds on a second species.**

### 1091

**And a propagated bound is REFUTED from outside, which is what the exercise was for.** *Our bound on K I nh is 0.0016–0.0112. Seaton with the published K⁺ polarisability α_d = 5.49(11) a₀³ gives **0.00036**; and Seaton under-predicts K I ng by 2.3× here — 0.00106 against a published 0.0024080 — because the dipole term omits the quadrupole α_q = 18 a₀⁵, so the scaled estimate is about 0.0008.* **Two independent estimates put K I nh below the compendium's deduced lower bound.**

### 1092

**That is register 1082's finding confirmed from outside rather than inferred.** *There, Al II and Si II's deduced lower bounds sat above Seaton's predictions and the argument rested on Seaton alone. Here the species has a published polarisability AND published defects, and both routes agree against the bound.* **The lower-bound propagation over-claims at high ℓ, and it took an external measurement to establish it rather than a second opinion from the same formula.**

### 1093

**ℛ places cells with great redundancy, and the redundancy is MEASURABLE and differs by index.** *Removing cells at random and asking whether ℛ puts them back: **Λ recovers exactly after removing 61%** — 9 of 10 trials, and 10 of 10 at 41%. **The spectra index tolerates about 25%** — 13 of 15 — and fails by 41%.* **Four hundred cells determine all 976 of Λ; the spectra index needs three quarters of itself.**

### 1094

**The difference is the number of coordinate pairs that actually constrain each other.** *Λ's coordinates are tightly coupled — ℓ < n, k ≤ 4ℓ+2, e ≤ k — so every envelope φ(i,j) carries a great deal and few cells reconstruct them. The spectra index has ONE constraint, charge < Z, and ℓ is free of both.* **The redundancy of an index under ℛ is set by its coordinate coupling, and that is a number one can compute before collecting anything.**

### 1095

**And from what is already measured, ℛ places four fifths of the rest.** *The 282 measured cells give |X| = 313 and |ℛ(X)| = 1,338, covering **1,307 of the index's 1,664 cells — 79%**.* **The conjecture that the operator locates any cell from those already established holds, for POSITION.**

### 1096

**What it does not do is VALUE them, and the two indices differ in whether that matters.** *A cell of Λ is an arrangement and carries no number, so recovering the cell recovers everything — which is why E(Λ) = 0 is a complete statement. A cell of the spectra index carries a defect, and that is its whole content.* **ℛ says K I nh exists and where it sits; it says nothing about whether the defect is 0.0008 or 0.0016.** *Registers 1078 and 1084 found a thousand cells with positions and no real bounds: the operator had done its job and the mechanisms had not.*

### 1097

**So the architecture is settled and stated: ℛ to place, mechanisms to value, and the coordinate coupling to say how much of an index is needed before the rest follows.** *That is how the equation works in each index, and the coupling is the quantity that varies between them.*

### 1098

**The index is propagated on the settled architecture and the two numbers are now separate.** *ℛ **places** 1,762 of 1,775 cells — **99.3%**, with only 13 unreachable. The mechanisms and Seaton together **value** 405 — **22.8%**: 285 measured, 68 two-sided from the mechanisms, 49 from Seaton alone, 3 from their intersection.* **927 cells are placed and carry a one-sided bound; 430 are placed and carry less.**

### 1099

**That gap between 99.3% and 22.8% is the whole finding of the day, in one line.** *The compendium reported 98.3% coverage this morning, and that figure was counting placement as though it were valuation.* **An index whose cells are located but not valued is a map with no elevations** — *true, useful, and not what the coverage number was claiming.*

### 1100

**The honest queue is now a valuation queue rather than a collection one.** *927 cells have a one-sided bound and need a second relation to close; 49 rest on Seaton alone and need either a measurement or a published polarisability; 3 have both and agree.* **Collection adds placements cheaply and valuations dearly, which is why the coverage figure rose so easily and the valued fraction did not.**

### 1101

**The consistency audit stopped working at register 1000 and nobody noticed for a hundred entries.** *Its number-word parser matched only "N hundred and M" — there was no case for thousands — so once the book's spelled total read "one thousand and three" the pattern failed to match, `cur` became a null sentinel, and the check coasted.* **It fired today only because "one thousand one hundred" broke it differently.** *Extended to read thousands, and the entry-number regexes widened from three digits to four; all twenty-two pass again.* **An audit that silently stops matching is worse than one that fails, and this one did both in sequence.**

### 1102

**Each relation is measured as a STEP rather than a bound, and most of them fail the test.** *The step is the ratio δ(source)/δ(target) on pairs where both are known, and what matters is its spread. **iso at s: median 1.21, geometric sd 1.23. iso at p: 1.18, sd 1.38.** Everything else scatters: ℓ at p, d, f gives sd **3.08 to 3.67**; elem gives **3.85 across all ℓ**.* **A relation that scatters by a factor of three per step cannot carry a value two cells** — *which is why the mechanisms have produced bounds and not values. That was a measurement, not a choice.*

### 1103

**Two steps survive, and the second only inside a filter.** *The isoelectronic step at s and p, with factors of 1.23 and 1.38. And the ℓ step at ℓ ≥ 4 in non-penetrating series, where register 1076 measured Seaton's ratio at **1.12** — the raw ℓ scatter of 3.67 is what happens when the penetrating and noise-floor pairs are left in.* **The filter is the difference between a usable step and an unusable one.**

### 1104

**Walking those two from every measured cell values 130 more, at a median accumulated factor of 1.23 and a worst of 2.05.** *Valuation rises from 313 cells to **443 of 1,664 — 27%**. By orbital: ns 37, np 38, nf 4, nh 11, ni 19, nk 21 — each axis reaching where it is strong.* **The walk halts itself when the accumulated factor passes 2.5**, so no cell is valued by a chain that has stopped saying anything.

### 1105

**And the walk corroborates register 1091's refutation independently.** *It gives Al II nh = **0.00761**, against Seaton's separately-computed 0.0070 and the compendium's deduced lower bound of 0.0083.* **Two routes agree with each other and against the bound** — *and the walk did not use Seaton's α for that cell, only the ℓ-ratio from Al II's own measured ng.*

### 1106

**The (Z, charge) plane has THREE directions and the walk used two.** *iso moves (Z,c) → (Z+1,c+1); elem moves (Z,c) → (Z,c+1); and **isocharge** — same charge state, next element, (Z,c) → (Z+1,c) — was never tested.* **Raw, it is the loosest of the three: median 0.82, geometric sd 4.12 across 123 pairs.**

### 1107

**And the diagonal was tight because it holds the ELECTRON COUNT still.** *(Z+1, c+1) keeps Z − c fixed. Register 1064 established the defect follows Nₑ^(1/3), so iso is the one move that does not disturb the variable the defect depends on; **isocharge and elem each change it by one.* **The index's natural coordinates are (Nₑ, charge, ℓ), not (Z, charge, ℓ)** — *and in that basis the three sds of 1.23, 4.12 and 3.09 stop being a puzzle.***

### 1108

**In the right basis the loose axis becomes the TIGHTEST step in the compendium.** *Dividing the Nₑ step by its Thomas–Fermi factor (Nₑ/(Nₑ+1))^(1/3) and restricting to s and p at Nₑ ≥ 9 leaves a residual scatter of **1.07** across 37 pairs — against iso's 1.23 and Seaton's 1.12. All ℓ and all Nₑ together give 2.36; the filter is what makes it usable.* **A raw ratio of 4.12 concealed a systematic of known form and a residual of 7%.**

### 1109

**The fourth step raises the walk from 130 cells to 209, and valuation from 27% to 31%.** *522 of 1,664 cells now carry a value, at a median accumulated factor of **1.17** — tighter than the three-step walk's 1.23 despite reaching 79 more cells.* **ns rises from 37 to 74 and np from 38 to 80**, which is where a penetration-dominated step should reach.

### 1110

**Three things were needed and none sufficed alone.** *The observation that the plane has three directions rather than two; the reparametrisation to (Nₑ, charge, ℓ), which says WHY the diagonal was tight; and Thomas–Fermi from register 1064, which supplies the factor.* **The step was always there. It was hidden because (Z, charge) is the wrong basis and a raw ratio mixes a strong systematic with its residual.**

### 1111

**A FIFTH step, and it needed no correction at all — only the filter.** *The elem step measured **3.85 across all ℓ and all Nₑ**. Restricted to s and p at Nₑ ≥ 9 it is **median 1.308, geometric sd 1.10 over 39 pairs** — usable raw.* **The same filter that made the Nₑ step usable makes the elem step usable too**, and neither needed a systematic removed; *the filter was doing the whole work.*

### 1112

**And dividing the ℓ step at p, d, f by Seaton's ratio makes it WORSE — 3.31 to 4.15.** *A polarisation formula applied to penetrating series does not merely fail to help; it adds scatter.* **That is the sharpest statement yet of register 1076's domain finding**, and it confirms the ℓ step cannot be rescued below ℓ = 4.

### 1113

**The five-step walk values 243 cells beyond the 313 measured — 556 of 1,664, 33%** — *at a median accumulated factor of **1.14**, tightening from 1.23 with three steps and 1.17 with four while reaching 113 more cells.* **213 of the 243 walked values are good to better than 30%.** *ns reaches 91 and np 97; the high-ℓ orbitals are unchanged at nf 4, nh 11, ni 19, nk 21, because only Seaton moves there.*

### 1114

**Every added step tightened the median rather than loosening it, which is the test that the additions are real.** *A walk that reached further by admitting worse steps would show the median factor rising. It fell at each addition: 1.23, 1.17, 1.14.* **The steps are being added in order of their measured tightness, and the walk chooses the least-error route to each cell**, so a new step is taken only where it beats what was already available.

### 1115

**The two smaller items resolve negatively, and for the same reason as the ℓ step.** *At Nₑ < 9 the ratio observed/Thomas-Fermi runs **0.616, 0.407, 0.722, 0.924, 0.995** across Nₑ = 2 to 6 — converging to unity but on 2 to 6 pairs each, and a free exponent fits at **k = 1.634 ± 1.244**, improving the residual from 1.60 to 1.58.* **And the charge step at d and f is loose rather than thin: sd 1.95 and 2.10, and the Nₑ ≥ 9 filter that unlocked three axes does nothing** — 1.92 against 2.00 at d, 2.09 against 1.86 at f.

### 1116

**Three failures, one cause: a step is usable where the physics has collapsed to ONE PARAMETER.** *At ℓ ≥ 4 the electron never enters the core and only the polarisability matters — Seaton, 1.12. At ℓ ≤ 1 with Nₑ ≥ 9 penetration is statistical and Thomas–Fermi governs — 1.07, 1.10, 1.23. **At ℓ = 2, 3 or Nₑ < 9 neither dominates**, and every correction tried leaves the scatter where it was: Seaton's ratio (worse), core-orbital counts (no better), defect magnitude (p = 0.34), a free TF exponent (1.60 to 1.58).* **The transition zone is not a missing systematic. It is the absence of one.**

### 1117

**So the remaining cells need measurement, and the measurement is ranked.** *Seeding each unvalued cell as if measured and re-walking: **777 of 1,139 would unlock at least one other cell, and 12 would unlock five or more**.* **The best are iron's s and p channels from Fe I to Fe VI — five cells each** — *because iron sits at Nₑ = 21 to 26 where all three penetration steps operate and its charge states chain through one another.* **Bismuth's high-ℓ channels unlock four each through Seaton.**

### 1118

**And the ceiling is now stated in the right terms.** *556 of 1,664 cells valued, 33%. Of the 1,139 unvalued, the great majority sit at ℓ = 2 or 3, or at Nₑ < 9, where no step exists.* **Further propagation cannot reach them and further collection must**, which is a different queue from the one the compendium has been keeping — *it wants channels chosen for what they unlock, not for what they fill.*

### 1119

**Today's spectra finding is carried into every index the book holds: REDUNDANCY UNDER ℛ, which had never been measured for any of them.** *Removing cells at random and asking whether ℛ puts them back: **Λ 61% · Λ_spectra 20% · Janet 0% · the periodic table 0% · the calendar 0% · a box ordering 0%**.*

### 1120

**And the conjecture that coordinate COUPLING explains it is REFUTED.** *Coupling — the fraction of ordered coordinate pairs whose envelope actually constrains — gives **r² = 0.002, p = 0.94** against redundancy.* **Janet and the box ordering both have 50% coupling and 0% redundancy; Λ_spectra has 17% coupling and 20% redundancy.** *The conjecture was mine, stated before the measurement, and it is wrong.*

### 1121

**What drives it is DIMENSION, and the projection test shows it on one object.** *Λ projected onto its own first d coordinates — same constraints throughout — gives **61% at d = 8, 30% at d = 7, 6 and 5, 5% at d = 4, and 0% at d = 3**.* **ℛ works on PAIRWISE envelopes, so an index of dimension d has d(d−1) of them: 56 for Λ, 6 for the spectra index, 2 for a plane.** *With two envelopes there is almost nothing to reconstruct from, and that is what the operator is rather than a fact about atoms.*

### 1122

**But only INDEPENDENT coordinates count, and that is the sharper half.** *Adding the electron count Nₑ = Z − c + 1 to the spectra index — **a function of two coordinates it already has** — drops redundancy from **20% to 0%**, while doubling the envelopes and raising coupling from 17% to 33%.* **A derived coordinate adds no information and obliges ℛ to reproduce it exactly, so recovery becomes strictly harder.** *Which is register 1107's reparametrisation seen from the other side: (Nₑ, charge, ℓ) is the right basis for VALUING cells and the wrong one for PLACING them.*

### 1123

**The redundancy finding is applied back to the spectra index, and it says the index is missing a coordinate.** *The channels carry a term symbol; the index collapses ¹S and ³S into one cell. Restoring multiplicity as a fourth INDEPENDENT coordinate takes redundancy from **20% to 61%** — level with Λ.* **Adding 2J instead gives 50%.** *The finding predicted this and the measurement confirms it: independence is what buys redundancy.*

### 1124

**And the same measurements place a factor of 4.7 more statements.** *In three coordinates, 316 measured cells let ℛ place **1,385 of 1,744 — 79%**. In four, 391 measured cells place **6,462 of 8,720 — 74%**.* **The percentage falls slightly and the count rises fivefold**, and each of the 6,462 is about a SPECIFIC TERM rather than an average over terms.

### 1125

**Which reframes what the compendium has been doing.** *Every figure computed at (Z, charge, ℓ) has averaged the singlet and the triplet — and register 987 showed those differ systematically, with the triplet defect exceeding the singlet in **22 of 22 ns cases**.* **The index has been averaging across a distinction its own mechanisms measured**, and the redundancy cost of doing so is a factor of three.

### 1126

**The cost of the change is that E rises fivefold and the valuation problem grows with it.** *8,720 cells against 1,744, with 391 measured rather than 316 — the term resolution is present in the data and was being discarded at the indexing step, not the measurement step.* **Whether to pay it is a decision about what the compendium is for**: an index that says less about more cells, or one that says more about each.

### 1127

**The index is rebuilt against the redundancy rule, and FOUR coordinates is the optimum.** *Five candidate axes are carried by the data and none is functionally derived from the others: Z, core charge, ℓ, multiplicity 2S+1, and 2J. Parent term appears on 9 channels of 596 and is too thin.* **On a controlled subset — the same elements, Z ≤ 16 — three coordinates give 0% redundancy, four give **82%**, and five give **0%** again.**

### 1128

**Adding J destroys what multiplicity buys, and the reason is register 1122 in a subtler form.** *My dependence test asked whether ℓ and S DETERMINE J. They do not. But |L−S| ≤ J ≤ L+S constrains it to 2·min(ℓ,S)+1 values of seventeen, so **J is not derived and is not independent enough**.* **A coordinate must be free, not merely undetermined.**

### 1129

**The entropy account of that is PARTIAL and is recorded as partial.** *Conditional entropy retained given the other axes: **Z 69% · ℓ 80% · charge 45% · 2J 27% · multiplicity 26%** — which does not separate multiplicity from 2J at all.* *On the cost side multiplicity buys 1.17 bits for a fivefold grid and 2J buys 1.03 for a 6.7-fold one, so the ratio favours multiplicity — but a ratio is not a mechanism, and **a collapse from 82% to 0% is sharper than any ratio explains**.* **The empirical result is solid and the account of it is not.**

### 1130

**So the reimagined spectra index is (Z, core charge, ℓ, multiplicity), four coordinates.** *It admits |L−S| ≤ J ≤ L+S as a CONSTRAINT on the cells it holds rather than as an axis, exactly as Λ carries ℓ < n and k ≤ 4ℓ+2 without making them coordinates.* **8,720 cells against 1,744, redundancy 61% against 20%, and 1,345 term-resolved values against 574 averaged ones** — *and the terms were always in the data, discarded at the indexing step.*

### 1131

**The general design rule the exercise produced.** *An axis earns a coordinate when it is independent of the others AND its distinct values are few relative to what it adds. Both conditions are necessary: a derived axis lowers redundancy (register 1122), and a merely-constrained axis with many values lowers it too.* **Λ obeys both — eight coordinates, each with three or four values, tied by constraints rather than by definition** — *which is why it recovers from 39% of itself and this index has not.*

### 1132

**The Method equation is ORDINAL and cannot be redefined to be otherwise.** *ℛ's envelopes are maxima: they say which cells are consistent with an ordering. A value is a magnitude, and no ordinal operator produces one.* **That is not a gap in the definition; it is what "order-theoretic" means** — *and register 1089 measured the consequence, ℛ with the defect as a coordinate giving bounds 2.5× looser than the mechanisms.*

### 1133

**So the method has FOUR parts, and three of them were running unnamed.** *𝒮 derives the STEP SET from the index itself. W is the VALUATION closure. ℛ is the PLACEMENT closure, the book's own. 𝒜 anchors by REDUNDANCY, keeping every route rather than the best one.* **And two defects rather than one: E(X) = |ℛ(X)| − |X| ordinal, E_W(X) = |W(X)| − |X| metric.** *For Λ the second is empty, which is why the book never needed it.*

### 1134

**W satisfies the closure axioms, which I expected it to fail.** *Extensive; **idempotent with exactly zero drift**, because the least-error route from the seed leaves nothing tighter to find; monotone except at one cell in 1,345.* **That exception is real and instructive: Mg II's ni is measured at exactly +0.0000, the Seaton step is multiplicative, and zero blocks the route to nk that a walked positive value would have opened.** *Adding a measurement can remove a walked cell.*

### 1135

**And testing 𝒮 exposed a circularity that must be forbidden.** *Re-deriving the step set from the WALKED result tightens iso at s from **1.13 on 43 measured pairs to 1.08 on 116 walked ones** — because the walked values were generated by that very step and agree with it perfectly. The step count goes **3 to 8**, and idempotence collapses: |W(W(X))| = 1,671 against |W(X)| = 558.* **𝒮 must be derived from MEASURED cells only, or the method confirms itself.**

### 1136

**𝒜 validates the whole construction from inside.** *956 cells are reached by more than one independent route. Their observed spread against the propagated estimate: **1.05 against 1.14, a ratio of 0.92**.* **The routes agree BETTER than the steps predict, so the walk's error bars are honest and slightly conservative** — *and this is the strongest check the valuation has had, because it comes from the index disagreeing with itself rather than from any outside formula.*

### 1137

**One honest limit of the automatic 𝒮.** *It finds three of the five steps derived by hand — the two isoelectronic ones and ℓ at s. The Thomas–Fermi Nₑ step at 1.07 and the elem step at 1.10 need the filter `s+p and Nₑ ≥ 9`, and 𝒮 does not know to look for one.* **An operator can measure a direction; it cannot discover that a direction is tight only on part of its domain.** *Register 1111 is what that looks like — the elem step read 3.85 until someone thought to restrict it.*

### 1139

**The multiplicity of a channel is DERIVABLE from the ground state, exactly.** *A channel is a core plus one Rydberg electron; the core's spin couples with s = ½, so 2S+1 ∈ {2(S_core±½)+1}, and S_core follows from aufbau filling by Hund's first rule.* **Tested on every electron count the compendium holds: 24 of 24 exact containment, 17 of 24 matching precisely**, the other seven being cases where only one of two allowed multiplicities has been captured.

### 1140

**So the index can be built from the ground state rather than from the sample, and it must be.** *The aufbau index over the same elements holds **8,488 cells against the sampled index's 4,220**, and admits **all 311 measured channels** where the sampled index admits only 296.* **The fifteen it excluded are Li III, Be IV and B V — one-electron ions with charge = Z — because the index's constraint has been `charge < Z` and should be `charge ≤ Z`.** *A standing error since construction, found by rebuilding.*

### 1141

**The ground state also supplies an EXCEPTIONLESS BOUND on every defect's integer part.** *floor(δ) ≤ min( p , n₀ − ℓ − 1 ) holds for **311 of 311**, where p is the core's orbital count at that ℓ and n₀ the first Pauli-allowed n — both from aufbau.* **As an equality it is right 57% of the time, and every error is negative.** *Within two of the bound: 303 of 311, 97%.*

### 1142

**n₀ is the periodic table's own coordinate and the index has never held it.** *n₀ − ℓ − 1 is the radial quantum number of the series' first member. The compendium records n as a RANGE on each channel and never as a coordinate.* **But it must not become one: n₀ is MONOTONE in the core, and register 1143 shows that is exactly the condition under which an axis must not be admitted.**

### 1143

**AN AXIS PRODUCED BY ANOTHER GIVES A DIMENSION EXACTLY WHEN ITS PRODUCTION IS NOT MONOTONE.** *Multiplicity is produced by Nₑ and NOT monotone in it — it cycles 2, {1,3}, 2, {1,3}, {2,4} — and adding it takes redundancy from **20% to 82%**. Nₑ is produced by (Z, charge) and monotone; adding it gives **0%**. n₀ is produced by (Z, charge, ℓ) and monotone; adding it gives **0%**.* **ℛ's envelopes are cumulative maxima, so a monotonically-produced axis is already inside them and adds cells without information; a non-monotone one is invisible to them and adds a dimension.** *This resolves registers 1122 and 1123, which appeared to contradict: derivation is not the criterion, MONOTONE derivation is.*

### 1144

**The compendium's scope changes from a collection to a survey.** *Built from aufbau across all 118 elements: **101,328 cells**, of which **63,193 have their integer part FORCED to zero by Pauli**, **35,852 are bounded within a window of three**, **929 are exact (one electron)**, **1,043 are walked** and **311 measured**.* **Three cells in a thousand are measured.** *The realistic verification frontier — stage ≤ VI and Z ≤ 92, roughly where analysed level data exists — is 7,792 cells, 8% of the survey.*

### 1145

**A single closed form is fitted over all 311 measured channels, using only atomic-index quantities.** *δ = [ B − q·e^(−a(Nₑ)ℓ)·e^(k/Nₑ)·c^g + C·c²/K(ℓ) ]·(1 + s·[triplet]), with B the derived bound, K Seaton's denominator, and a(Nₑ) = A₀ + A₁Nₑ^(−1/3) + A₂/Nₑ.* **rms 0.2321, R² 0.9317, median error 0.090** — *and by orbital: **0.0148 at g, 0.118 at f**, 0.24–0.28 at s, p, d.*

### 1146

**The equation converts the bottleneck from transcription to search.** *A capture yields one channel from thirty levels and a limit fit. A PUBLISHED DEFECT is one number and tests the equation directly — and every precision-Rydberg paper reports δ₀ for its series.* **Tested against Na I ng, K I ng, nf, nd, ns, Sr I ns, np, nd and Cr I ns — four elements, none captured — the errors run from **0.0006 at ng** to **1.38 at Sr I nd**.**

### 1147

**And a published number localises WHICH term is wrong, which a capture does not.** *K I's measured δ_d/δ_s = 0.127 implies a decay constant of 1.03; Sr I's 0.730 implies 0.157. The fitted 2.17 was a compromise fitting neither.* **The decay is set by the atom's SIZE: a against ln Nₑ gives r² = 0.437 across 56 species, against w (electrons beyond the noble gas) only 0.143, and against charge nothing at all (p = 0.34).**

### 1148

**A structural flaw remains and my repair made it worse.** *Sr I nd has B = 2 and a measured δ = 2.38 — the defect EXCEEDS the bound, which floor(δ) ≤ B permits since δ may reach B + 1. But the equation's penetration term is always negative, so it can never produce δ > B.* Separating deficit from fraction should fix it, and **the attempt failed**: it gave rms 0.3105 against 0.2321 and drove the polarisability NEGATIVE, the optimiser finding a degenerate corner in a non-smooth objective. *Version 2 stands, and the flaw is recorded rather than patched.*

### 1149

**And the press leaks markup when a line BEGINS with a bold marker, which no register had triggered until now.** *Entry 1148's bold spans were balanced and the audit still failed: the closing `**` reached the PDF because the opening one sat at the start of its line.* **`artefact_audit` caught it on the first build after the entry was written** — *the leak is a formatting fault of my own making and the audit is the only thing that would have found it, since the register reads correctly as text.***

### 1150

**A channel is not a number. It is a curve, and the compendium has used one end of it.** *Fitting the Ritz form δ(n) = δ₀ + δ₂/(n−δ₀)² to every series with four or more members — 274 of 596 — the δ₂ term removes **48% of what the compendium has been calling scatter**: mean spread 0.0199 without it, mean residual 0.0104 with it.* **Every threshold built on spread — the step accuracies, the joint-fit gate, the lowest-rms limit rule, the walk's halt — measured a mixture of noise and structure.**

### 1151

**And δ₂ is reached by nothing the index holds.** *Against ln Nₑ, ℓ and charge together, δ₀ gives R² = 0.549 and δ(n₀) — the channel's other end — gives 0.517. **The curvature between them gives 0.018**, with a coefficient of variation of 14.7.* **δ₀ is explained to 55% and the shape to 2%**, and no combination of the two ends is invariant: sum 0.539, product 0.368, difference 0.018.

### 1152

**The contamination is a HIGH-ℓ effect, and it acts where the compendium was most confident.** *It scales as δ₂/(n²δ₀), so at s with δ₀ ≈ 2 it is a part in a thousand and at f with δ₀ ≈ 0.01 it is a tenth.* **Re-measuring every step on clean δ₀: iso at f goes 2.06 → 1.22 and becomes usable; ℓ at f goes 4.55 → 2.29.** *Five of eight steps tightened, and both large moves are at f — where Seaton operates and where the walk does its cleanest work.*

### 1153

**THE ISOELECTRONIC STEP MOVES A CHANNEL RIGIDLY; NO OTHER DIRECTION DOES.** *Measuring both coordinates' ratios separately: iso gives δ₀ 1.194 and δ₂ 0.859 at s, 1.150/0.979 at p, 0.858/0.907 at d, 0.561/0.627 at f — **the two scale together at every ℓ**. The ℓ step gives 1.427/0.752 at s, 3.696/1.373 at p, 8.536/5.264 at d — **the defect and the curvature change by different factors, and increasingly so as ℓ falls**.* **Along a sequence the channel translates; along ℓ it deforms.**

### 1154

**Which explains a failure rather than relocating it, for the first time today.** *The ℓ step below ℓ = 4 resisted Seaton's ratio, core-orbital counts, defect magnitude, a free Thomas–Fermi exponent and a valence term — five corrections, none of which moved it.* **A scalar ratio cannot represent a transformation that changes a channel's shape**, and that is what the ℓ direction does.

### 1155

**But the hopeful reading is refuted: ℓ is not a SHEAR either.** *Fitted as a 2×2 map on the pair, it improves on the scalar by **14% at s→p and 1% beyond**, with relative residuals of 0.30 to 0.97.* **The ℓ step is not a linear transformation of (δ₀, δ₂) at all**, and the two-coordinate rebuild locates the difficulty without dissolving it.

### 1156

**The standing position after eleven registers on one line.** *One direction of the index is an isometry of the channel and the others are not. δ₂ is half of every error bar and is determined by nothing the index carries. The Ritz refit must be run on the full capture set before any threshold downstream is trusted.* **That is a session's work and it is the right next one** — *because until it is done, every accuracy figure in the compendium is measured against a quantity that is not noise.*

### 1157

**THE SIGN OF δ₂ IS A COORDINATE, AND IT IS THE FIRST ONE THE GROUND STATE CANNOT SUPPLY.** *Seaton requires δ₂ < 0 for a polarisation series, so a positive δ₂ says the channel is not what the formula describes. Across 274 channels: **s 76% positive, p 74%, d 37%, f 6%, g 7%, h 9%**.* **The sign partitions the compendium into two populations with different physics and different error scales — median raw spread 0.0159 against 0.0029, median fit residual 0.0058 against 0.0003, U-test p < 10⁻⁵.**

### 1158

**And it names the transition zone exactly.** *np is 66% penetrating, **nd is 35%** and nf 9%.* **ℓ = 2 is the only orbital where the two populations sit together in comparable number**, and every step measured there has been averaging two physics — *which is why five separate corrections to the ℓ step failed and why the walk could never reach nd.*

### 1159

**The MAGNITUDE of δ₂ is a sixth coordinate and it does a different job: it predicts the channel's own scatter at R² = 0.761.** *Against ℓ alone at 0.230 and the sign at 0.267 — and adding the sign to the magnitude adds **nothing**, 0.761 to 0.761.* **The sign says which physics; the magnitude says how well the channel is determined.**

### 1160

**Which makes |δ₂| a better gate than the spread the compendium currently uses.** *Every threshold — the joint-fit precondition, the two-member gate, the walk's halt at 2.5 — tests the raw spread, and register 1150 established the spread is **48% δ₂ by construction**.* **A gate on |δ₂| is not circular: the spread is an outcome, δ₂ is a fitted parameter of the channel's own curve.**

### 1161

**The three quantities do NOT separate, and that is the structural finding rather than a shortfall.** *δ₀ against |δ₂| gives r² = 0.270; the sign against δ₀ gives 0.240.* **They are three views of one coupled system — nucleus, core, Rydberg electron — and no two of them are orthogonal.** *Which is the reason δ₂ resisted every occupancy-derived predictor in register 1156: an occupancy count is a ONE-BODY statement about the core, and δ₂ is a TWO-BODY statement about core and electron together.*

### 1162

**So the index has coordinates of two kinds and the survey's premise is qualified.** *Z, charge, ℓ and multiplicity are DERIVED — the ground state gives all four for all 118 elements, 101,328 cells. The regime and the magnitude class are MEASURED, and nothing derives them.* **A cell's regime can be guessed at 91% for ℓ ≥ 3 and 75% for ℓ ≤ 1, and NOT AT ALL at ℓ = 2** — *which is the row that has resisted every method tried today.*

### 1163

**The index is finished, and it carries a regime assignment for every cell.** *101,328 cells: **63,193 forced · 35,852 bounded · 1,043 walked · 929 exact · 311 measured**, of which **179 carry a fitted Ritz pair and therefore a MEASURED regime**.* **By regime: 62,664 polarising at a 91–94% prior, 24,952 penetrating at 74–76%, and 12,472 MIXED** — *the ℓ = 2 band, where no prior exists because the populations are 37/63 and neither dominates.*

### 1164

**Which is the index's own statement of where it does not know its own physics.** *Every other cell can be assigned a regime with a stated confidence from ℓ alone. The 12,472 at ℓ = 2 cannot.* **That is 12.3% of the survey, and it is the same 12.3% that resisted the ℓ step, the deficit, the decay constant, the transition zone and the curvature.** *Five failures, one band, now named.*

### 1169

**Which is a LANGUAGE result, and register 761's caution generalises.** *Statistics cannot state a closure defect. **Analysis cannot state an ordering** — least squares has no rank in it. And a purely multiplicative algebra cannot state an EXCEPTION: fitted multiplicatively the same data gives **205/205, 143/143, 66/66** where the measurements give 194, 89 and 55.* **The additive form cannot see the rule; the multiplicative form cannot see the exceptions; each is blind in the way its language is blind.**

### 1171

**And it works.** *ln δ = ln A + β·ln(B+1) − a·ℓ + μ·ln Nₑ + γ·ln c + σ[triplet] + ρ[regime] + ρ_ℓ[regime]·ℓ.* **P.lcollapse 205/205 → 204/205 against a measured 194. P.iso 143/143 → 129/143 against 89. Exchange 66/66 → 61/66 against 55. And the fit improves: ln-R² 0.8026 → 0.8164.** *Still too monotone, and the remaining gap is how many regime-like coordinates are needed rather than whether the form can work.*

### 1165

**Λ_α is built as an INDEX rather than a table, and it catches a fault on the first build.** *Coordinates Z · Nₑ(core) · n_out · ℓ_out, the last two derived from Nₑ by aufbau and both non-monotone in it. 18 cores held, E = 10.* **Sorted by (n_out, ℓ_out), α must FALL with Z along an isoelectronic sequence — and the Ne-like and Mg-like rows obey it while the Ar-like row does not: K I 5.490 published, Ca II 6.665 extracted, Sc III 4.705.** *A table would have listed 6.665 beside 5.490 and said nothing; the index put them on a row where the ordering is a physical requirement.*

### 1166

**The equation's polarisation term was DEAD, and Λ_α revived it.** *Seaton's term is 3α·c²/K(ℓ) with α per species; the equation carried C·c²/K(ℓ) with C = 0.0078 universal, forcing α = 0.0026 a₀³ on every core where the real values run 0.07 to 26.* **With α supplied as a label the ℓ ≥ 4 rms falls from 0.01504 to 0.00958 — 36% — and below ℓ = 4 the term must be gated OFF entirely**, since K(ℓ) is small there and applying it drives the fit to rms 39.3.

### 1167

**Against twelve published values never fitted on, the equation is exact above ℓ = 3 and rough below.** *Median error **0.00155 at ℓ ≥ 3** — Na I ng −0.0003, K I ng −0.0016, K I nf −0.0121 — and **0.368 below**.* **Across all 311 measured channels: rms 0.2449, R² 0.924, and by orbital 0.283 at s falling to 0.0096 at g.** *Half the index is computable to a hundredth, and that half is where the physics collapsed to one parameter.*

### 1168

**THE CONTAINMENT HIERARCHY, AND IT RUNS BACKWARDS FROM EVERY ASSUMPTION.** *A level sits in a channel, a channel in a spectrum, a spectrum in an element, an element in a sequence — and every mechanism operates at exactly one of those levels. Their scatters: **within a channel (δ₂) unmeasured and 48% of all scatter · within a spectrum (ℓ) 3.31 · within an element (charge) 1.10 · along a sequence (Z,c) 1.23 · across sequences (Nₑ) 1.07**.* **The INNERMOST moves are the LOOSEST.** *A sequence step changes nucleus and charge together, holding the electron count, so the core's structure is unchanged and only its scale moves — a similarity transformation. An ℓ step changes which part of a fixed core the electron samples. The tight steps move the whole system rigidly; the loose ones move the electron through a fixed core.*

### 1170

**And it surfaces THREE STANDING CONTRADICTIONS the compendium has been carrying unnamed.** *One index, two languages, two answers: δ falls with ℓ — **order 194/205, analysis 102/205**. The triplet exceeds the singlet — **order 55/66, analysis 33/66**. δ falls along a sequence — **order 89/143, analysis 135/143**.* **The cypher says order and analysis absorb an addition identically and agree on Λ. On Λ_spectra they do not, and a disagreement between languages is the one thing the cypher forbids.**

### 1172

**And it reports five language/index pairs never run.** *Λ_spectra has been read in ORDER and ANALYSIS only; geometry, algebra, information and statistics have never touched it. Λ_α has been read in order alone.* **The cypher's agreement — six languages, all ten pairs — is established on Λ's 976 cells and asserted everywhere else.**

### 1173

**LOGIC IS NOT A LANGUAGE. It is the mechanism by which any language answers a binary question about a cell.** *Three levels, not one list: **binary** is the type — a cell is admitted or it is not; a **language** is a coordinate system with a closure operator; **logic** is binary → language → binary.* **A language earns its row when logic can operate on it and get a binary back** — *which is why documentary has no row: it returns a citation. The book's arithmetic is then exact: five operator-bearing languages give C(5,2) = 10 combinations, plus statistics as a sixth and documentary as a seventh.*

### 1174

**The statistics operator is max-entropy on the PAIRWISE marginals, and my first attempt used first-order ones.** *At order 1 it admits all 6,912 cells of Λ's ambient; at order 2 it returns exactly 976, E = 0, reproducing ℛ cell for cell. IPF converges to the max-entropy distribution matching the specified marginals (Deming & Stephan 1940; Ireland & Kullback 1968), and which marginals is the whole question.* **My earlier report that the book's caveat 'does not reproduce' was an artefact of the wrong marginal order.**

### 1175

**AN INDEX NEEDS THREE COORDINATES BEFORE ITS LANGUAGES CAN DISAGREE.** *At two there is one pair, so pairwise consistency and the cell coincide and every language returns the same answer for no reason.* **The periodic table, Janet and the calendar were all being tested at two and all reported 'agree'.** *Rebuilt at three — block, ℓ and weekday respectively, each non-monotone in the second coordinate — the periodic table gives order E = 100 against statistics 0, reproducing the book's recorded caveat exactly. All three match the book at 2-D first: 36, 0 and 7.*

### 1176

**And the cypher analysis then returns a theorem-shaped result: E(X) = 0 if and only if the languages agree.** *Six indexes, three operators — order, statistics and geometry — and the agreement tracks closure without exception. **Λ and a box ordering: E = 0 and every pair agrees. The periodic table, Janet, the calendar and Λ_spectra: E > 0 and every pair differs.** * **Closure has been an order-theoretic property; it is also a language-theoretic one, and the second test is cheaper — ℛ enumerates the ambient product, pairwise consistency needs only the marginals.**

### 1177

**The whole-object E decomposes into faces and CORNERS, and 36% is corner.** *Of the 6,195 cells ℛ admits and Λ_spectra does not hold, 3,993 are admitted by some three-axis slice and **2,202 by none**.* **Statistics admits ONE of the 2,202 and geometry 28%, against 20% and 70% of the faces** — *so the corners are an artefact of loose coordinatisation, not a feature. And every available fifth coordinate makes them worse, by 70% to 652%, because all four candidates are DERIVED.*

### 1178

**The index was under-CONSTRAINED, not under-coordinatised, and the missing constraint was one the compendium had already proved.** *Applying register 1139's rule — the multiplicity must be one Hund allows for the core — cuts **E(order) from 6,195 to 2,879, statistics from 806 to 429, geometry from 3,773 to 1,984**, and the corners from 2,202 to 963.* **A result proved in one place and never carried into the operator that needed it was costing half the defect in every language at once.**

### 1179

**What remains after that is COLLECTION, not constraint, and the cypher analysis names it without ambiguity.** *Of the 2,879 cells still admitted, 2,450 fail some pairwise marginal, and the largest violation is **Z × charge: the index holds 70 of the 182 element–charge pairs its alphabets allow, and the 112 it lacks let in 1,935 cells**. Every one of the 112 is physically possible.* **Ti VI, K III, Sc V, Ca III, N IV, Ne V, Al V, Fe IV — 24 cells each, and all exist.**

### 1180

**But 'the data is published' is only half true, and the other half is the parent term.** *A closed-shell core has ONE parent and gives one Rydberg series per ℓ. **Fe IV's 3d⁴ core carries sixteen LS terms**, and the capture confirms it: 13 parents appear, 24 distinct (parent, ℓ, term) series, **and every one has exactly one member**.* **Fe IV has ~1,000 analysed levels and no extractable defect — the levels are identified and the SERIES are not separable.** *So the 112 split: closed-shell pairs are collection gaps; open-shell pairs are outside what a quantum-defect index can hold at all.*

### 1181

**FIVE OUT-OF-SAMPLE CAPTURES, AND THE FIRST TWO REFUTE THE GATE.** *N IV (Be-like, one parent, 2s.ns through 2s.nf, n = 3–9) gives δ_d = **0.0335** where the `B/(B+1)` gate demands exactly zero — N IV's core is 1s²2s¹ with no d orbitals. **Ti IV** (argon core, published limit 348,973.3 ± 1.5) gives δ_d = **0.6202** and δ_f = **0.0774**, both where the gate demands zero.* **Ca IV adds a third at 0.553.** *Three species, cores with no orbitals of that ℓ, and substantial defects in every one.*

### 1182

**The gate improved the fit by 14% and caused 70% of what remained.** *`B/(B+1)` forces δ = 0 on **111 measured channels** whose defects run 0.011 to 0.908, median 0.060; Σδ² over them is 6.65, contributing 0.146 to an rms of 0.208.* **It was right about the INTEGER part and wrong about the FRACTION** — *those 111 all have |δ| < 1 and no integer part to bound, and the gate killed their fraction along with it. Register 910's split, arrived at for the fourth time.*

### 1183

**The ladder is not a rival to the equation; it is a FORM whose parameters were never closed.** *δ(c) = A + B·ln(c+1)/c fitted per (Nₑ, ℓ, multiplicity) gives median rms **0.0083** across 52 sequences — twenty times better than any closed form of its parameters.* **And on Ti IV it beat the equation 4 of 4 and on N IV 3 of 3**, *from three fitted points extrapolated one step.*

### 1184

**A IS NOT TO BE PREDICTED. IT IS CALIBRATED TO THE PERIODIC INDEX.** *As c → ∞ at fixed Nₑ the core collapses to a point charge and the ion is hydrogenic: δ → 0. That is the one-electron column's own edge, not a fit.* **Fixing A ≡ 0 costs 2.4× in the per-sequence fit and RAISES B's predictability from R² 0.761 to 0.877**, *because A had been absorbing structure that belongs to B. The ladder becomes one parameter: δ = B·ln(c+1)/c with B = −0.6645 + 0.5906·Nₑ^⅓ − 0.0780·ℓ + 0.5917·p − 0.0247·[triplet] — five mechanisms the compendium measured separately, as five terms of one line.*

### 1185

**Sr II was chosen to PROVE the closed ladder and it refuted it, which is worth more.** *Limit 88,965.18 ± 0.02, nine ns members, ten nd, nine nf. Measured **s 2.7113 · p 2.3501 · d 1.4577 · f 0.0618 · g 0.0098**, spreads 0.008 to 0.032.* **Predicted 2.016 / 1.648 / 0.955 / 0.587 / 0.545 — low by 0.70 at s, p, d and HIGH by 0.53 at f and g.** *Ti IV showed the same signature at half the size, so the ℓ-tilt is systematic and grows with Nₑ.*

### 1186

**p is not a TERM in the equation. It is the ARGUMENT.** *Species sharing a core-orbital vector share a defect profile: Hg II and Bi III both read (6,4,3,1) and agree to 5%; Ca II and K I both read (3,2,0,0) and both collapse at ℓ = 2; Sr II reads (4,3,1,0) and its f falls off the cliff exactly where the 0 sits.* **Fitting δ = a·p^e·Nₑ^k·ln(c+1)/c gives held-out rms 0.255 on Sr II and Ti IV, against ~0.50 for the closed ladder** — *and same-ℓ counting beats 'orbitals at or below ℓ' by a factor of three, which is the opposite of what I had argued twice.*

### 1187

**ORBITAL COLLAPSE IS THE MISSING DISCRIMINATOR, AND ITS THRESHOLD IS A JANET BLOCK BOUNDARY.** *Ti IV's nd and Sr II's nf both have p = 0 and their defects differ by a factor of ten — 0.620 against 0.062. What differs is that Ti (Z = 22) is past the 3d collapse and Sr (Z = 38) is far below the 4f.* **Measured across 116 p = 0 channels at ℓ = 2 or 3: collapsed median 0.637, uncollapsed 0.036, U-test p = 9.8×10⁻⁴.**

### 1188

**And the thresholds ARE the Janet boundaries, exactly, three times.** *The n+ℓ = 5 block opens at Z = 21 (Sc) and 3d collapses at 21. The n+ℓ = 7 block opens at 57 (La) and 4f collapses at 57. The n+ℓ = 8 block opens at 89 (Ac) and 5f at 89.* **What K, Ca and Sc have in common is that they span a single n+ℓ boundary** — *K is 4s¹, Ca closes the 4s block, Sc opens the 3d block, and the 3d orbital contracts across exactly that span.* **This is why Janet closes at E = 0 and the classroom table does not: Janet's coordinate IS n+ℓ, so its blocks are the collapse boundaries, and the classroom table splits the 3d block across two periods and hides the boundary the physics uses.**

### 1189

**The largest outliers are the atoms APPROACHING a boundary, not past it.** *Ca I nd = 0.908 at Z = 20 against a threshold of 21; Ba II nf = 0.756 at Z = 56 against 57; Ca II 0.634 and K I 0.246.* **The collapse is a rapid transition, not a step, and Ca I nd is the pre-collapse maximum of the whole compendium.** *Ba II independently confirms the 57 one shell up.*

### 1190

**The Janet term closed the largest error in the compendium's predictions.** *Adding it: Ti IV nd goes from **−0.620 (gate) and −0.489 (polarisation) to −0.056**. Overall rms 0.1825 → **0.1411**, R² 0.9583 → **0.9739**, held-out 0.2203 → **0.1503**.* **The collapse coordinate is read off the periodic table, not fitted** — *one lookup, and it separates two channels that p = 0 could not.*

### 1191

**THE INDEX BY EXISTENCE STATUS, AND NOTHING IS IMPOSSIBLE.** *101,328 cells: **1,265 verified** (336 measured, 929 exact by symmetry), **2,935 possible** (the ion exists and the series separates), **97,128 improbable**, and **ZERO impossible**.* **The survey was built from aufbau with the multiplicity constraint already applied, so its 247,248 forbidden cells were excluded at construction** — *the mathematics has no interior contradictions left to find, and every remaining question is about access.*

### 1192

**The improbable 97,128 break down, and charge alone is 64% of the index.** *No analysed Rydberg data above charge 10: **61,748**. Element too short-lived, Z > 103: **24,312**. Series unresolved above ng: 5,367. ### 1249

**THE LÖWDIN CHALLENGE TAKEN UP: WHY DOES THE n+ℓ RULE HOLD?** *Löwdin 1969 named the derivation a major unsolved problem; Klechkovsky 1962, Demkov & Ostrovsky 1972, Wong 1979, Ostrovsky 2001 and Allen & Knight 2002 have all attempted it, and Scerri's commentary finds the last inadequate.* **The nearest thing to a derivation is Demkov & Ostrovsky, n+ℓ filling rule in the periodic system and focusing potentials, Sov. Phys. JETP 35 (1972) 66-69** — *a potential class whose levels depend only on n+ℓ — and the consensus is that a chosen potential is not what Löwdin intended.*

### 1250

**THE MEASURED DEFECTS REPRODUCE THE MADELUNG ORDERING, AND THE COMPENDIUM'S OWN EQUATION PRODUCES THE FILLING SEQUENCE.** *n∗ = n − δ orders by n+ℓ in **608 of 626 pairs, 97.1%**, against 81.5% for raw n — the defect contributes 15.6 points. And the channel equation, whose inputs are p (Pauli), Nₑ^k (Thomas–Fermi) and ln(c+1)/c (Edlén) and which never mentions n+ℓ, **picks the subshell aufbau fills at 97 of 101 elements.*** **The four failures are Y, La, Lu and Ac — the four block openings, where the collapse branch does the work and that branch is the equation's weakest term.**

### 1251

**THE 18 ORDERING FAILURES ARE ALL ONE ℓ-PAIR IN IONS.** *Every one is 4s against 3d, and every failing species carries charge 2 or more: Ar II, Sc III, P III, Si III, P IV, S IV, Ca IV, Ti IV, S V, Ca IX.* **Neutral atoms: 120 of 120 pairs, exceptionless. Ions: 488 of 506.** *Fisher p = 0.032; the s–d gap falls from a median +0.844 in neutrals to +0.260 in ions, Mann–Whitney p = 0.019. The degradation is a STEP between charge 1 and 2, not a slope — which is why the linear tests returned p = 0.55 and p = 0.22 and the dichotomy returns 0.032.* **And it matches Theodosiou, Manson & Inokuti 1986 independently: the closed shells move from noble-gas numbers at z = 1 to hydrogenic at z ≥ 3.**

### 1252

**THE ORTHOGONALITY COUNT APPEARS TWICE WITH OPPOSITE SIGN, AND ALMOST CANCELS.** *n₀ = p + ℓ + 1 because p core orbitals of the same ℓ force p nodes and an nℓ function has n−ℓ−1 of them. And δ tracks p with slope one: at charge 1 the measured slopes are **0.807 at s, 0.973 at p, 0.992 at d**, r² 0.86 to 0.96.* **So n∗ = n₀ − δ is nearly independent of p** — *penetrating channels cluster at n∗ ≈ 2.4 with an ℓ-slope of +0.171, while non-penetrating ones sit at **n∗ = ℓ + 1 to r² 0.973**, medians 2.926, 3.978, 4.996 against 3, 4, 5.*

### 1253

**THE CYPHER READING SUPPLIES THE MISSING STEP: THE ORDER LANGUAGE ALREADY HELD IT.** *Q.bound says floor(δ) ≤ p, exceptionless on 328 channels — an ORDER statement. dδ/dp = 1 is the ANALYSIS statement. The two agree exactly where the bound SATURATES, and saturation is checkable in the order language alone.* **It saturates at high ℓ: floor(δ) = p in 153 of 167 channels at d, f and g — 92%. At s it never does, 3 of 86.** *So dδ/dp = 1 is not a measurement there; it is an identity showing through.*

### 1254

**AND THE SHORTFALL IS AN INTEGER FUNCTION WITH NO PARAMETER.** *The shortfall grows one per core shell and caps: **2 at s, 1 at p, 0 at d and f.** So floor(δ) = p − min(p, max(2−ℓ, 0)), which is **282 of 325 exact, 27 low by one, 16 high by one, none off by two**.* **max(2−ℓ,0) counts the core shells of that ℓ with n ≤ 2** — *the K and L shells, where the field is still nearly −Z/r, so those nodes are hydrogenic and cost nothing. Only s and p have orbitals there. And every miss is a floor() crossing near an integer driven by charge, not a wrong node count: the −1 cases are P IV, S V, Ca IX, Ti XI, all at Nₑ = 12 with δ squeezed below 1 by Edlén's fall.*

### 1255

**THE FRACTIONAL PART IS NOT A RESIDUE: IT IS THE PHASE FROM ONE INTERACTION, AND IT HAS A GATE.** *Tested against every candidate coordinate, frac(δ) is carried by the CORE CONFIGURATION and not by the parent term — closed against open core explains 1.7% of its variance and the multiplicity moves it by 0.043 against a spread of 0.318, while (ℓ, core configuration) explains 54.3%.* **And the core's OUTERMOST SUBSHELL alone recovers 85% of that.** *The rule: **frac(δ) ≈ 0 when ℓ − ℓ_core ≥ 2** — 123 channels, median 0.017 against 0.327 below the gate, Mann–Whitney p = 2.2×10⁻²⁰, and 90 of the 123 have δ < 0.05 outright. A Rydberg electron two units of angular momentum above the core's outermost is centrifugally excluded from it and stays hydrogenic.*

### 1256

**WHAT IS DERIVED AND WHAT IS NOT, STATED PLAINLY.** *Derived and parameter-free: n₀ = p+ℓ+1; floor(δ) = p − min(p, max(2−ℓ,0)); frac(δ) ≈ 0 above the centrifugal gate; n∗ = ℓ+1 for non-penetrating channels.* **Measured and not derived: frac(δ) BELOW the gate — and that is what separates 4s from 4p.** *So the chain reproduces the FILLING SEQUENCE at 96% of elements and does not reproduce the full energy ordering of all subshells: n∗(np) < n∗(ns) always, because the integer decides and it decides against Madelung for 3d against 4p. The 96% survives only because 3d and 4p never compete for the same electron. **Löwdin asked for the second, and this is the first.***

### 1257

The load-bearing step below the gate is empirical, and Ostrovsky's standing objection to every claimed solution — that such approaches "usually require some empirical information" — applies to this one.* **What is here is an independent empirical confirmation, on 325 real channels, of the mechanism Demkov & Ostrovsky's model potential encodes** — *arrived at by measurement rather than by choosing a potential, with the integer half now parameter-free.*

### 1259

**AND IT REFUTED THE LADDER'S UNIVERSALITY.** *δ(c) = B·ln(c+1)/c gave r² 0.9948 to 0.9999 on every light sequence and **0.61 at s, 0.33 at p, and NEGATIVE at d and f** on this one. Sr II's 4d is 1.4592 against Rb I's 1.3307 and Y III's 1.3965 — it RISES then falls, which a monotone form cannot do. And f rises monotonically, 0.014 → 0.061 → 0.147.* **But B against p held: slope +1.116, r² 0.9415, against +1.163 from the eight-sequence fit — two independent estimates of the same coefficient from disjoint data.**

### 1260

**THE TWO LADDERS, AND WHAT MAKES d AND f DIFFERENT.** *An ℓ ≥ 2 orbital with no core orbital of its own ℓ faces a centrifugal barrier that splits the potential into two wells (Connerade, ch. 5; arXiv:2402.02609). Below its threshold it sits in the OUTER well and raising the charge pulls it inward, so δ RISES. s and p have no barrier, no outer well, and only the screening ladder.* **Tested across every sequence: rising sequences lie entirely below their collapse threshold (median fraction 1.00) against 0.71 for falling ones, Mann–Whitney p = 0.024.** *Nₑ = 19 spans the 3d threshold at 21 and has the largest positive slope, +0.114; Nₑ = 37 reaches the 4d threshold at 39 and gives +0.033.*

### 1261

**THE FOUR REGIMES, AND THEIR BOUNDARIES AS EQUATIONS.** *From two integers — p, the core's orbital count at this ℓ, and n_out, the principal number of the core's outermost subshell:* **regime 1 (p ≥ 1, n₀ > n_out) the electron STARTS a new shell, 99 channels; regime 2 (p ≥ 1, n₀ ≤ n_out) it COMPLETES the current one, 24; regime 3 (p = 0, Z < T) outer well uncollapsed, 142; regime 4 (p = 0, Z ≥ T) collapsed, 18.** *The 1|2 boundary is a shell boundary; the 2|4 boundary is n₀ < n_out, where the orbital lies radially INSIDE the core's outermost shell — Y at Z = 39, Ac at 89; the 3|4 boundary is Z = T.* **Regime 2 is the p-block: Al, Si, P, S at ℓ = 1, and Rb, Sr, Y, Ba at ℓ = 2 where the shell is about to collapse.**

### 1262

**THE COLLAPSE SWITCH, MEASURED.** *Charge-normalising the outer-well d channels by (Nₑ−1)/Nₑ·√Nₑ·(charge term) gives y = 0.086 at D = −2 (K I), 0.291 at −1 (Ca I, Ca II), 0.342 at 0 (Sc III), 0.373 at +1 (Ti IV) — a factor of 3.4 in one proton, then a plateau.* **h(d) = 0.40, centre D = −1.5, width 0.40, read from the table rather than fitted** — *the least-squares fit ran away to h = 3387 because 49 of 53 channels sit far below the threshold and dominate the residual.* **Using the measured switch closed Z = 21.**

### 1263

**AND h(f) FROM PUBLISHED RADII, NOT FROM A DEFECT.** *arXiv:2402.02609: the collapsed and uncollapsed f wavefunctions are BOTH NODELESS, so the collapse is pure phase and h is the inner-well defect. For a nodeless state ⟨r⟩ = (3n∗² − ℓ(ℓ+1))/2Z_c.* **Ba's hydrogenic 4f at ⟨r⟩ = 18 a₀ gives δ = 0.000 EXACTLY — the formula validating itself — and La's collapsed 4f at 0.7 a₀ gives δ = 1.887, whence h(f) = 0.468.** *No published nf quantum defect near a collapse threshold exists; the radius collapse is documented and the defect is not.*

### 1264

**THE LA / CE CAPTURES LOCATE THE 4f COLLAPSE TO ONE PROTON.** *La II's ground is 5d² with 4f.5d at +16599 cm⁻¹; Ce III's ground is 4f² with 4f.5d at +3277. **Between Z = 57 and Z = 58 the 4f/5d ordering inverts.*** *Y II gives the same at 4d: 5s² ground with 4d.5s at +840, against Zr III's 4d² ground.* **And read as isoelectronic ladders rather than isolated species, both are one statement: at fixed electron count the ground configuration flips between charge 2 and charge 3** — *Nₑ = 20: 4s² → 3d4s → 3d²; Nₑ = 38: 5s² → 5s² → 4d²; Nₑ = 56: 6s² → 5d² → 4f²; Nₑ = 88: 7s² → 6d7s → 6d².* **Four electron counts, four different nuclear charges, one ionisation stage. The invariant is the CHARGE, which is Theodosiou, Manson & Inokuti 1986 exactly.**

### 1266

**THE CHARGE DEPENDENCE COLLAPSES AT HIGH ELECTRON COUNT.** *Successive ratios along the mercury sequence are 1.050 and 1.051 — δ ∝ c^(−0.14). Every candidate form predicts far steeper: ln(c+1)/c gives 1.189, c^(−½) 1.225, 1/(c+1) 1.333, 1/c 1.500.* **Fitting δ ∝ c^(−x) within each sequence, x falls monotonically with electron count: 0.66 at Nₑ = 3, 0.50 at 11, 0.47 at 12, 0.39 at 13, 0.31 at 19, 0.21 at 37, and 0.141 at 80.** *So ln(c+1)/c was never general — over c = 1 to 4 it falls as c^(−0.39), and 0.39 is the value of x near Nₑ = 13, which is exactly where it was calibrated. A Rydberg electron outside eighty others barely notices one more unit of core charge; outside three it notices a great deal.*

### 1267

**AND THE CARRIER FOR x(Nₑ) IS A POWER LAW, NOT A LOGARITHM.** *x₀ + x₁·ln Nₑ fits the sixteen penetrating measurements slightly better — wrms 0.0546 against 0.0653 — and gives x(80) = 0.068 against the measured 0.141, then **crosses zero at Nₑ ≈ 118**, which would make δ RISE with charge for every heavy species. **A charge exponent cannot be negative: the form is structurally wrong, not badly calibrated.*** *β·Nₑ^(−α) with β = 1.1594, α = 0.4251 gives x(80) = 0.180. Neither hits 0.141; the measurement sits between them.* **Four forms fit the calibration set identically and differ only in extrapolation — the data cannot choose, and the Nₑ = 80 anchor is what discriminates.**

### 1268

**p AND Nₑ ARE ONE COORDINATE, NOT TWO.** *ln(p·Nₑ) alone explains r² 0.8887 of ln δ; ln p and ln Nₑ separately give 0.8892 — a difference of 0.0005. And the two free exponents come out 0.509 and 0.553, the same number twice.* **p is a step function of Nₑ, its steps being the shell openings, and the correlation of ln p with ln Nₑ is 0.95 at s, 0.92 at p, 0.77 at d.** *So the product form √p·Nₑ^k was over-parameterised, and the honest form is √(p·Nₑ).*

### 1269

**THOMAS–FERMI IS REFUTED HERE, AND ITS FAILURE GIVES THE ½.** *TF predicts δ ∝ Z^(1/3) with ℓ entering only through (ℓ+½)²Z^(−2/3). TF gives ⅓ because it sets r_core ~ Z^(−1/3), the atom shrinking as Z grows. Atoms do not shrink — atomic radii are near-constant across the table — and with r_core constant the same integral gives δ ∝ √Z ≈ √Nₑ.** *That is the ½, derived.*

### 1270

**AND NO CENTRIFUGAL CORRECTION TO THE PHASE SURVIVES.** *Three barrier forms tested — −b(ℓ+½)²/√(pNₑ), √(pNₑ − b(ℓ+½)²), exp(−b(ℓ+½)²/(pNₑ)) — **all give b < 0**, which would increase δ at high ℓ, and all change rms by 0.003 on 123 channels.* **The barrier's whole role is in WHETHER the electron gets in — the gate, p = 0 against p ≥ 1 — and not in how much phase it accumulates once inside. ℓ enters only through p.**

### 1271

**THE FORM AS IT STANDS, AND THE ONE FREE NUMBER.** *δ = A·√(p·Nₑ)·c^(−β·Nₑ^(−α)) for penetrating channels, with A = 0.2579, β = 1.1594, α = 0.4251: **123 channels, rms 0.1667, R² 0.9689**. ### 1272

**A DISCIPLINE, EARNED BY LOSING IT REPEATEDLY.** *Every joint refit today moved three quantities at once and I could not tell which was real: refitting with the regime factor drove x(Nₑ) from 0.86 − 0.18lnNₑ to 0.36 − 0.03lnNₑ and the factor from 1.234 to 1.029, the two absorbing each other.* **Anything measured independently is LOCKED and never refitted; only genuinely free numbers are fitted; and a refit moves ONE thing at a time.** *With that rule the residuals become a diagnosis rather than noise — and the first thing they said is that the regime-2 factor of 1.234, which I had called four independent confirmations, is 1.09 once x(Nₑ) is held fixed. **They were four measurements of the same absorption, not four confirmations.***

### 1273

**AND A FAULT OF MINE, RECORDED.** *I presented n∗ = ½(n+ℓ+1) + p/2 − δ as a result. It is an IDENTITY — substituting n₀ = p+ℓ+1 and n+ℓ = p+2ℓ+1 returns n∗ = n₀ − δ.* **The 96.8% of n∗'s variance "explained by n+ℓ" is largely circular, since both are dominated by n₀ and δ is small against it; the slope of ½ follows arithmetically because n+ℓ grows twice as fast in ℓ as n₀ does; and a = ½ for a bare core is the identity evaluated at p = 0, δ = 0.** *None of it is evidence that nature organises on n+ℓ. The test that would be evidence — whether n∗ correlates with n+ℓ better than with n₀ alone — has not been run.*

### 1274

**WITHDRAWN: THE REFUTATION OF THOMAS–FERMI AT REGISTER 1269, AND THE ½ AT 1271.** *Both rested on an Nₑ exponent of 0.539 measured WITH ln(c+1)/c as the charge term — the form since shown to be structurally wrong. With the corrected charge form the exponent is 0.3876, against Thomas–Fermi's ⅓.* **The charge term was contaminating the Nₑ exponent, and I refuted a theory on a wrong variable.** *The WKB form √(Z·r_core) is right; the core-radius scaling r_core ∝ Nₑ^(−0.225) is measured and sits between constant and Thomas–Fermi, nearer the latter.*

### 1275

**THE COORDINATE MUST RUN WITH ITS PARENTS.** *Plugging δ into Λ_spectra as a fifth coordinate costs 45–47% of what a random coordinate costs, at every resolution — δ falls with charge while p and Nₑ rise, so ℛ's monotone envelopes cannot express it.* **n∗ = n₀ − δ rises with both and costs 24–30%.** *And measured per element rather than pooled the order reverses completely: n∗ costs 0.327 against n₀'s 0.266, while δ costs 1.695 — worse than noise. **Pooling was measuring differences BETWEEN atoms, which is what the equation is for; inside one atom n∗ is nearly a derived coordinate and δ is not.***

### 1276

**STEP 1 · ONE EQUATION PER ELEMENT.** *Within a species only ℓ varies and p is fixed by the ground configuration, so the natural form is **δ = a·√p** with one constant.* **41 species fitted, 22 with R² > 0.8, a running 0.066 to 1.654.** *The grid is monotone without exception: every column rises with Nₑ, every row falls with charge.*

### 1277

**STEP 2 · WHAT THE 41 SHARE AND HOW THEY DIFFER.** *They share the FORM exactly — δ = a√p, with p read and never fitted. **AND THE k-DRIFT FALLS OUT WITH NO CROSS TERM.** *k(c) = ∂ln a/∂ln Nₑ = 1.3620 − 0.3499·u, and u falls as c rises, so k rises with c automatically: predicted 0.332, 0.626, 0.735, 0.816 against measured 0.572, 0.705, 0.828, 1.132.* **The direction and ordering are right and the magnitudes are low at both ends** — *the quadratic captures the mechanism of the drift and not yet its full size.*

### 1285

**THE ℓ-SPREAD LAW, STATED AND THEN CORRECTED THE SAME DAY.** *First fitted on six hand-picked species as spread = 0.113·(u − 2.5), r² 0.868, p = 0.007.* **On all nineteen species with three or more penetrating channels it gives r² 0.044 in u and is not significant.** *The lattice caught it by asking for the same law in another carrier: in p it gives **slope −0.069, r² 0.356, p = 0.007**, and with both offered u's coefficient collapses to +0.006.* **√p is WORST when the core has few shells of that ℓ and best when it has many, becoming exact near p ≈ 5.4 — the opposite of what I first stated.** *Six points chosen because they looked orderly is the same error as the four "independent confirmations" of 1.23.*

**THE CHARGE EXPONENT IS SELF-REFERENTIAL, AND ITS CONSTANT IS ONE.** *Testing whether x runs in u rather than Nₑ: **e^(−u/2) gives r² 0.9121 against 1/√Nₑ's 0.8343**, and the constant falls from C = 1.322 ± 0.284 to **C′ = 1.0065 ± 0.179**.* **So x = e^(−u/2) = c^(1/3)/√Nₑ, and δ ∝ c^(−x) means the exponent of c contains c: ln δ ⊃ −c^(1/3)·ln c/√Nₑ.** *A fitted constant became unity by changing carrier — the charge sets the rate at which its own influence decays.*

### 1287

**THE CONSTANT INDEX, AND WHAT IT SAYS.** *Fourteen constants on (role, carrier, standing, arity): three fitted, six measured, five derived or attributed.* **Every CENTRE is a small integer or half-integer — 2 for the free shells, 2 for the gate, −1.5 for the switch, 2.5 for the ℓ-validity, and u₀ ≈ 4. Every SCALE is not.** *And β = ⅔ is the only constant of arity three, appearing in the amplitude, the exponent and the validity — the load-bearing constant of the system, and the one that is attributed.*

### 1489

So the literature sets diff(S) aside knowingly, not by oversight.* **M.C2 IS THEREFORE CLOSEABLE IN THREE DIMENSIONS AND BLOCKED IN FOUR BY AN OPEN PROBLEM IN THE THEORY OF DIFFEOMORPHISM GROUPS RATHER THAN BY ANYTHING PHYSICAL. ### 1490

**WHY THE ORBIT CLASSIFICATION WORKS IN ONE DIMENSION AND NOT TWO — AND WHY THE BLOCKER MAY NOT APPLY TO US.** *The person asked to explore the theory and say why it does and does not work for us. The reason it works on S¹ is a single accident of dimension one.* **A coadjoint vector of Diff⁺(S¹) is a quadratic differential b(θ)dθ², which defines a canonical second-order ODE — HILL'S EQUATION ψ″ + bψ = 0 — whose solution space is two-dimensional, so going once around the circle gives a MONODROMY in SL(2,ℝ), a single element of a three-dimensional Lie group whose conjugacy classes are a short list. An infinite-dimensional orbit problem collapses onto a finite one, and Witten's list is that collapse read off.** *On S² there is no canonical ODE, because a two-manifold has no distinguished direction to run one along; with no ODE there is no monodromy and no finite-dimensional invariant to conjugate. Nor is there a Virasoro to lean on — Vect(S¹) has its one-dimensional central extension and Vect(S²) does not have the analogue — so the Kirillov–Kostant machinery has nothing to grip. THE FAILURE IS NOT DIFFICULTY BUT THE ABSENCE OF THE OBJECT THE PROOF IS ABOUT.* **And the matrix regularisation halves the problem without closing it: sl(N,ℂ)'s coadjoint orbits are classified at finite N, but whether the classification survives N → ∞ is unestablished, and it covers sdiff(S²) only — by Hodge, what it misses is the gradient part, another whole function's worth, since Moser makes Diff/SDiff the infinite-dimensional space of normalised volume forms.** *BUT THE BLOCKER MAY NOT APPLY TO US, AND MACKEY'S CONSTRUCTION IS WHY. Coadjoint orbits of a semidirect product G ⋉ N are built in two steps: an orbit of G on the DUAL of N, then a coadjoint orbit of the STABILISER. Step one for us is Diff(S²) acting on maps from S² into the three-dimensional dual of sl(2,ℝ) — reparameterisation of the source, which is singularity theory and not the open problem. Step two needs the unclassified object only where the stabiliser is CONTINUOUS, and a generic map has trivial or finite stabiliser.* **So for generic corner data no coadjoint orbit of Diff(S²) is ever required, and the d = 4 blocker would be an artefact of asking for more than the problem needs. This is MY inference from the semidirect structure and no source states it. Three things must hold and none is checked — that the dual really is those maps, that generic stabilisers really are finite, and that the physical corner data is GENERIC. Black hole horizons are famously not generic, Kerr being axisymmetric, and that is the objection most likely to sink it.**

The projection is badly lossy and the coordinates cannot be read off the value.** *THE WEAK READING — that the structure leaves a TRACE — holds for three of four. Against chance the lifts are Z 2.81, ℓ 1.50, charge 1.32, and multiplicity 1.02, which is nothing at all.* **AND I MUST FLAG Z's 2.81 AGAINST MYSELF. It is the largest lift here and register 1581 found Z the WEAKEST coordinate at 2.1 per cent of within-ℓ variance. They measure different things and do not conflict, but the lift is INFLATED because Z has twenty-nine values and chance is therefore only 4.8 per cent. A LARGE LIFT ON A LOW BASE IS NOT A STRONG SIGNAL — 13.4 per cent accuracy is the honest number and it is poor.** *The clean result is the multiplicity. A lift of 1.02 means THE SCALAR CARRIES NO TRACE OF SPIN AT ALL, and that is now the THIRD independent measure saying multiplicity does not behave like the other three: register 1607 found it moving the WRONG WAY under the penetration split, better in the non-penetrating regime where every other axis is worse; register 1597 found it unkeyable in 313 of 369 species.* **SO WHAT THE ATOM'S ONE NUMBER REMEMBERS OF ITS OWN STRUCTURE IS: THE NUCLEUS A LITTLE, THE ANGULAR MOMENTUM A LITTLE, THE CHARGE LESS, AND THE SPIN NOT AT ALL.**

### 1626

**MULTIPLICITY MOVES BETWEEN PROBLEMS RATHER THAN WITHIN ONE, WHICH EXPLAINS ALL THREE FAILURES — AND RECODING IT FIXES NOTHING.** *Row 15 asked why multiplicity fails three independent tests. Looking for one cause rather than three.* **THE CAUSE IS IN WHAT ITS VALUES MEAN. Z, charge and ℓ are properties of ONE OBJECT varying along their own axes, and every value is the same kind of thing. 2S+1 is not: a doublet is ONE electron outside a closed shell, a singlet is TWO paired, a triplet is TWO parallel, a quartet is THREE. STEPPING ALONG THE MULTIPLICITY AXIS CHANGES THE NUMBER OF BODIES IN THE PROBLEM.** *The other three axes move within one problem; this one moves BETWEEN problems. That is a single cause for all three failures — the wrong-way behaviour under the penetration split at register 1607, the unkeyability in 313 of 369 species at 1597, and the absent trace in the scalar at 1625.* **AND THE OBVIOUS REMEDY FAILS. Recoding as a VALENCE COUNT — doublet to one electron, singlet and triplet both to two, quartet to three — gives a lift of 1.08 against multiplicity's 1.02, on a base of 47 per cent against 34. SIX HUNDREDTHS OF A LIFT. And merging singlet with triplet is what register 1622 says is correct at high n, because the channels mix; it still buys nothing.** *The purity test returned no number at all for the valence count, and that is the honest output rather than a failure: the count is a FUNCTION of 2S+1, so holding the other coordinates fixed and stepping along it yields no comparable pairs. IT IS NOT AN INDEPENDENT AXIS BUT A COARSENING OF THE ONE IT WAS MEANT TO REPLACE, and a coarsening cannot be more monotone than what it coarsens.* **AND `A.cert` SAYS WHY IN ONE LINE. A coarsening is a RELABEL, which is an admitted operation — and admitted operations do not add information, they rename it. To separate the one-body problem from the two-body one you would have to SPLIT THE INDEX, and register 1608 already showed that partitioning Λ_spectra destroys the closure it has.**
